title: The benefits of solitude, with Thuy-vy Nguyen, PhD, and Netta Weinstein, PhD

sentences.en: For some people, the word solitude conjures up images of monks, hermits, wilderness retreats, and other extreme examples of spending time alone.
sentences.zh: 对于某些人来说，独处这个词会让人联想到僧侣、隐士、荒野隐居处以及其他极端独自度过时光的例子。

sentences.en: But in reality, solitude is a common, maybe even an everyday experience.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，独处是一种很常见、甚至可能是每天都会经历的事情。

sentences.en: Some research has found that the average American adult spends up to one-third of their waking hours alone.
sentences.zh: 一些研究发现，美国成年人平均每天有高达三分之一的清醒时间是在独处中度过的。

sentences.en: In recent years, psychologists have been exploring how these hours spent on our own affect us, including the potential benefits as well as the challenges of solitude.
sentences.zh: 近年来，心理学家一直在探讨这些独自度过的时间是如何影响我们的，包括独处的潜在益处以及面临的挑战。

sentences.en: And they're finding that being alone can offer us a needed opportunity for rest and reflection.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，独自一人可以为我们提供急需的休息和反思的机会。

sentences.en: So what is the difference between loneliness and being alone?
sentences.zh: 那么，孤独感（loneliness）和独自一人（being alone）有什么区别呢？

sentences.en: Do you have to be physically alone to experience solitude, or can you be alone in a crowd?
sentences.zh: 体验独处必须身体上独自一人，还是说你可以在人群中感到独处？

sentences.en: How does alone time affect our emotions and stress levels?
sentences.zh: 独处时间如何影响我们的情绪和压力水平？

sentences.en: Why do some people seem to crave solitude more than others do?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些人似乎比其他人更渴望独处？

sentences.en: And how can we balance the need for solitude with fostering the social connections that are essential for mental health?
sentences.zh: 我们又该如何在对独处的需求与培养对心理健康至关重要的社交联系之间取得平衡呢？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the relationship between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学话你知》（Speaking of Psychology），这是美国心理学协会的旗舰播客，主要探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的关系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。

sentences.en: We have two guests today.
sentences.zh: 我们今天请到了两位嘉宾。

sentences.en: First is Dr. Thuyvi Nguyen, an Associate Professor of Psychology and Principal Investigator of the Solitude Lab at the University of Durham in the UK.
sentences.zh: 第一位是崔维·阮博士（Dr. Thuyvi Nguyen），她是英国杜伦大学心理学副教授兼独处实验室（Solitude Lab）首席研究员。

sentences.en: She and her colleagues study how spending time alone affects people's mood, stress levels, sense of loneliness, and more.
sentences.zh: 她和同事们研究独自度过时间如何影响人们的情绪、压力水平、孤独感等等。

sentences.en: She's interested in exploring both the positive and negative aspects of spending time alone and how we can all have healthier relationships with solitude.
sentences.zh: 她对探索独自度过时光的积极和消极方面，以及我们如何与独处建立更健康的联系很感兴趣。

sentences.en: Next is Dr. Netta Weinstein, a Professor of Psychology at the University of Reading in the UK.
sentences.zh: 接下来是内塔·温斯坦博士（Dr. Netta Weinstein），她是英国雷丁大学心理学教授。

sentences.en: She's also Director of the European Research Council's SOAR project, which stands for Solitude, Alone, But Resilient.
sentences.zh: 她还担任欧洲研究理事会“SOAR”项目的负责人，该项目代表“独处、孤身一人却充满韧性”（Solitude, Alone, But Resilient）。

sentences.en: Dr. Weinstein has a background in clinical and social psychology and studies the role that motivation plays in shaping behavior and well-being.
sentences.zh: 温斯坦博士拥有临床和社会心理学背景，主要研究动机在塑造行为和幸福感方面所起的作用。

sentences.en: Dr. Nguyen, Dr. Weinstein, thank you for joining me.
sentences.zh: 阮博士、温斯坦博士，非常感谢二位参加节目。

sentences.en: Thank you for having us on.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我们来。

sentences.en: Yeah, thank you for having us.
sentences.zh: 对，谢谢邀请我们。

sentences.en: I should also mention that you both, along with journalist and researcher Heather Hansen, are co-authors of a new book called Solitude, The Science and Power of Being Alone,
sentences.zh: 我还要提一下，二位与记者兼研究员海瑟·汉森（Heather Hansen）共同合著了一本新书，书名为《独处：独处的力量与科学》（Solitude, The Science and Power of Being Alone），

sentences.en: published in April by Cambridge University Press.
sentences.zh: 该书于4月由剑桥大学出版社出版。

sentences.en: So let's start by talking about the distinction between solitude and loneliness.
sentences.zh: 那么我们先来谈谈独处与孤独感之间的区别。

sentences.en: How do you define solitude in the work that you do?
sentences.zh: 在你们开展的研究中，是如何定义独处的？

sentences.en: When we study solitude, we're talking kind of simply about the state of being physically alone, having nobody around, and not interacting with anybody digitally or in person.
sentences.zh: 当我们研究独处时，其实很简单，指的是身体上独自一人的状态，身边没有任何人，也没有通过数字设备或面对面与任何人互动。

sentences.en: So when we tend to talk about solitude, it's simply the experience of being alone, the state of being alone.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们倾向于谈论独处时，它就是单纯独自一人的体验、独自一人的状态。

sentences.en: Now, what about the distinction between solitude and loneliness?
sentences.zh: 那么，独处和孤独感之间有什么区别呢？

sentences.en: There's been a lot of public discussion lately about loneliness in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 最近社会上有很多关于美国人孤独感的讨论。

sentences.en: Our Surgeon General, Dr. Vivek Murthy, released a report last year calling out a loneliness epidemic among Americans.
sentences.zh: 我们的卫生总监维韦克·穆尔蒂医生（Dr. Vivek Murthy）去年发布了一份报告，指出美国人中存在孤独流行病。

sentences.en: But you make the point in your book that solitude is not the same as loneliness.
sentences.zh: 但你们在书中指出，独处并不等同于孤独感。

sentences.en: So how do they differ?
sentences.zh: 那么它们有何不同？

sentences.en: So after the definition that Nada has given us,
sentences.zh: 所以在内塔给出了定义之后，

sentences.en: very much loneliness is more related to our social experience.
sentences.zh: 孤独感在很大程度上与我们的社交体验更相关。

sentences.en: So that's usually how the best way for us to explain to people is because when we see that our social experience in reality doesn't match with our expectation.
sentences.zh: 所以这通常是我们向人们解释的最佳方式，因为我们发现现实中的社交体验与我们的期望不符。

sentences.en: So with that definition of loneliness, then it's easy for people to distinguish between solitude, which is just a state of when you're not interacting with another person,
sentences.zh: 因此，有了孤独感的这个定义，人们就很容易区分独处（即你没有与其他人互动的状态），

sentences.en: and when you feel lonely, and that is when you feel like the social world doesn't match with what you want it to be.
sentences.zh: 以及当你感到孤独时的状态——也就是你觉得社交世界不符合你的期望的时候。

sentences.en: And I think just to add a little bit to that, I think one of the important things that we tend to forget
sentences.zh: 我想在此基础上补充一点，我认为我们往往容易忘记的一个重要事情是，

sentences.en: is we can feel lonely when we're in solitude, but we can also feel lonely when we're with other people.
sentences.zh: 我们可以在独处时感到孤独，但我们也可以在与其他人在一起时感到孤独。

sentences.en: So actually, if you think about the emotion of loneliness, negative emotion, it signals that we're disconnected.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，如果你想想孤独感这种情绪（一种负面情绪），它发出的信号是我们脱节了。

sentences.en: It's not something that's unique to solitude.
sentences.zh: 这不是独处所特有的。

sentences.en: It's something that can happen whether or not we're with people.
sentences.zh: 无论我们是否与人在一起，这种情况都可能发生。

sentences.en: So Dr. Nguyen, you've done lab studies where you've looked at how spending even a brief period of time alone affects people's emotions and state of mind.
sentences.zh: 阮博士，你做过实验室研究，探讨过哪怕只是短暂的独处如何影响人们的情绪和心态。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that research?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这项研究吗？

sentences.en: What did you find?
sentences.zh: 你们发现了什么？

sentences.en: Basically, when we try to put people into the lab, we decide like a short period so that we can study just the effect of solitude on people's emotions.
sentences.zh: 基本上，当我们试图把人们请进实验室时，我们设定了一个很短的时间，这样我们就能专门研究独处对人们情绪的影响。

sentences.en: So I want to make it clear that the decision of just pick a very short period,
sentences.zh: 所以我想澄清的是，之所以决定只选择一个非常短暂的时间，

sentences.en: either 15 to 30 minutes, is so that we can distinguish from other phenomenon that people have studied.
sentences.zh: 也就是15到30分钟，是为了将其与人们研究过的其他现象区分开来。

sentences.en: Things like isolation or loneliness is usually researcher studies those concepts in longer period from four hours for young people to 10 hours for an average adult.
sentences.zh: 诸如隔离或孤独感之类的事情，研究人员通常会研究较长时间的概念，年轻人从4小时到普通成年人的10小时不等。

sentences.en: So when I put people in the room for just 15 to 30 minutes, what we often observe is how we have different emotion, different type of emotion.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我把人们关在房间里仅仅15到30分钟时，我们经常观察到的是我们如何产生不同的情绪、不同类型的情绪。

sentences.en: In psychologists, we often think of emotion as two dimensions.
sentences.zh: 在心理学中，我们通常认为情绪有两个维度。

sentences.en: One is either go from negative emotion to positive emotion, which is generally what we tend to think of emotions.
sentences.zh: 一个是消极情绪到积极情绪，这通常是我们倾向于认为的情绪。

sentences.en: But there's also another dimension is from the low inactivation and high inactivation, or low in arousal or high in arousal.
sentences.zh: 但还有另一个维度，即低激活度到高激活度，或者低唤醒度到高唤醒度。

sentences.en: So the beginning of all these lab studies, we tend to just see that the emotions that are high in arousal drop after we spend those brief period of solitude.
sentences.zh: 所以在所有这些实验室研究的初期，我们往往会发现，在经历这些短暂的独处之后，高唤醒度的情绪会下降。

sentences.en: And then sometimes we also see some of the low arousal type of emotion.
sentences.zh: 有时我们也会看到一些低唤醒度的情绪。

sentences.en: So we're talking about calm and relaxation also goes up.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们所说的平静和放松也会增加。

sentences.en: And when I mentioned earlier about those strong, high arousal emotion, we're talking about things like excitement, energizations,
sentences.zh: 当我刚才提到那些强烈的高唤醒度情绪时，我们指的是兴奋、充满活力等事情，

sentences.en: things that you can imagine experience at like a party or a concert.
sentences.zh: 也就是你能在派对或音乐会上体验到的那种感觉。

sentences.en: But it's also include emotion like anger, anxiety as well.
sentences.zh: 但它也包括愤怒、焦虑等情绪。

sentences.en: So when we think about the effect of solitude, previous research tend to focus more on the drop in those high energy, positive emotion, and we forget that solitude can also help us
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们思考独处的影响时，先前的研究往往更关注那些高能量、积极情绪的下降，而我们忘记了独处也可以帮助我们

sentences.en: to calm down those strong negative emotion as well.
sentences.zh: 平复那些强烈负面情绪。

sentences.en: So that's including our anxiety, stress, anger.
sentences.zh: 这包括我们的焦虑、压力和愤怒。

sentences.en: But can't you feel strong emotions when you're alone, when you're in solitude?
sentences.zh: 但是，当你独自一人、处于独处状态时，难道你就不能感受到强烈的情绪吗？

sentences.en: That's a possibility.
sentences.zh: 这是有可能的。

sentences.en: And that's why researchers like on the topic of solitude, we tend to try to identify situation where those strong emotion can come up.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么研究独处的研究人员倾向于试图找出那些强烈情绪会出现的情境。

sentences.en: And usually those are when people might have negative thoughts or ruminative thoughts that arise when they spend time alone.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，那是在人们独处时产生消极想法或反刍思维的时候。

sentences.en: But the tricky part is sometimes I also find evidence in the recent work that people tend to prefer solitude when they experience those strong negative emotion.
sentences.zh: 但棘手的是，有时我也在最近的工作中发现证据表明，当人们经历这些强烈的负面情绪时，他们往往更倾向于独处。

sentences.en: So we don't know if it is solitude that create those emotion or people going into solitude when they experience those emotion with the purpose to kind of calm themselves down.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不知道是独处产生了这些情绪，还是人们在体验这些情绪时为了平复自己而进入独处状态。

sentences.en: So that is an empirical question we need to look at next.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个我们需要在接下来探讨的实证问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I see you nodding, Dr. Weinstein.
sentences.zh: 我看到你在点头，温斯坦博士。

sentences.en: This all resonates with you.
sentences.zh: 这一切都引发了你的共鸣。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是的。

sentences.en: You know, I think just like social interactions, we'll often think about having these great relationships, great conversations with other people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为就像社交互动一样，我们经常会想到与其他人建立这些美好的关系、进行美好的对话。

sentences.en: You know, those conversations that leave us feeling excited and happy or angry or more relaxed.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那些让我们感到兴奋和快乐，或者愤怒或更放松的对话。

sentences.en: And in a way, solitude's a little complicated in much the same way that relationships are.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，独处有点复杂，其方式与人际关系非常相似。

sentences.en: You know, we can have strong feelings in solitude.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们在独处时会有强烈的情感。

sentences.en: It might help to bring us a sense of calm, but it doesn't mean it always will.
sentences.zh: 它可能有助于给我们带来平静感，但这并不意味着它总是如此。

sentences.en: And what we bring into it is really important.
sentences.zh: 而我们带入其中的东西真的很重要。

sentences.en: And certainly how we experience it, you know, what we're doing in those moments, how we're thinking, how we're dealing with our own emotions,
sentences.zh: 当然，我们如何体验它，你知道，我们在那些时刻在做什么，我们是如何思考的，我们是如何处理自己的情绪的，

sentences.en: all of those things are going to shape the solitude experience, much in the same way that they shape our relationships with other people.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都会塑造独处的体验，就像它们塑造我们与他人的关系一样。

sentences.en: Are there some emotions that you would never feel in solitude?
sentences.zh: 有没有一些情绪是你永远不会在独处时感受到的？

sentences.en: For example, I've read that when you're by yourself, you can't be embarrassed.
sentences.zh: 例如，我读到过当你独自一人时，你不会感到尴尬。

sentences.en: I mean, is that true?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是真的吗？

sentences.en: I think in the literature, there's distinguished between also social emotions.
sentences.zh: 我认为在文献中，也有对社会情绪的区分。

sentences.en: So I definitely, I don't think that we have looked at it.
sentences.zh: 所以我绝对、不认为我们已经研究过这一点。

sentences.en: But for example, even when I collect data, I try to kind of think about also some emotion that if we give participants, it would not be possible for them to answer the question.
sentences.zh: 但例如，甚至自我收集数据时，我也会试着去考虑一些情绪，如果我们将它们呈现给参与者，他们将无法回答这个问题。

sentences.en: Things like, for example, embarrassed.
sentences.zh: 比如，例如，尴尬。

sentences.en: I think sometimes things like shame is also questionable, feeling ashamed.
sentences.zh: 我认为有时像羞耻感也是值得商榷的，即感到羞愧。

sentences.en: But I don't discount that.
sentences.zh: 但我并不排除这种可能。

sentences.en: Sometimes we might feel ashamed when we feel alone, if we kind of recount those experiences.
sentences.zh: 有时当我们回想起那些经历时，如果我们感到孤独，我们可能会感到羞愧。

sentences.en: And if I can just add, because I think it's a fascinating question, and it sort of speaks to what happens to us, what our internal experience is when we're in solitude.
sentences.zh: 如果我能补充一点，因为我认为这是一个引人入胜的问题，它在某种程度上说明了当我们处于独处状态时，我们会发生什么，我们的内在体验是什么。

sentences.en: Because I think one of the things that we're finding is that we do carry the experiences that we have into solitude, and even ones that we don't often think of.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为我们发现的一点是，我们确实把我们的经历带入了独处之中，甚至是我们通常不会想到的经历。

sentences.en: So one of the sort of surprising findings in some of the daily diary studies, where we ask people kind of about how is your solitude today?
sentences.zh: 因此，在一些日常日记研究中，有一个令人惊讶的发现，我们询问人们关于你今天的独处情况如何？

sentences.en: What kind of experiences did you have?
sentences.zh: 你有哪些体验？

sentences.en: What kind of emotions did you have?
sentences.zh: 你有哪些情绪？

sentences.en: And what we find is that even when we look at things like relatedness to other people, or that sense of social connection, that we take that social connection into solitude,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，即使当我们观察诸如与他人的关联感或社交连接感之类的事情时，我们也会将这种社交连接带入独处中，

sentences.en: so we can still be in solitude and feel connected to other people.
sentences.zh: 所以我们仍然可以在独处的同时感到与他人有连接。

sentences.en: And it speaks to, you know, I think this is an area where we really need more evidence,
sentences.zh: 这说明了，你知道，我认为这是一个我们确实需要更多证据的领域，

sentences.en: but it sort of speaks to the possibility that a lot of those relationships and interactions we have, that we're carrying those memories,
sentences.zh: 但这在某种程度上说明了这种可能性：我们拥有的许多关系和互动，我们正带着这些记忆，

sentences.en: we're carrying the kind of symbolized people in our lives into our solitude space.
sentences.zh: 我们正把生命中那些符号化的人带入我们的独处空间。

sentences.en: And so we might reflect back to something we did that maybe felt, you know, shameful to us or was embarrassing, and recall and kind of recreate that emotion in the solitude space,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们可能会回想起我们做过的事情，这些事情也许让我们觉得（你知道的）羞耻或尴尬，并在独处空间中回忆并重新创造那种情绪，

sentences.en: even when there's nobody there to sort of give us more of that feeling.
sentences.zh: 即使周围没有人给我们带来更多那种感觉。

sentences.en: Many people feel uncomfortable with the idea of going out to dinner or to a movie by themselves, even if they might enjoy it.
sentences.zh: 许多人对于自己一个人出去吃晚餐或看电影的想法感到不自在，即使他们可能会很享受。

sentences.en: Why do you think that there's some stigma around the idea of solitude, of being out in public alone?
sentences.zh: 你认为为什么围绕着独处、独自一人在公共场合出现这种想法存在一些污名化？

sentences.en: So in the book, we kind of cover some of the historical context that might shape our schema or the norms that we usually carry about this experience called solitude.
sentences.zh: 所以在书中，我们探讨了一些历史背景，这些背景可能会塑造我们对这种被称为独处的体验的图式或通常遵循的规范。

sentences.en: We talk about how, like, historically, we tend to see solitude talked about as more of a form of punishment.
sentences.zh: 我们谈到历史上人们倾向于将独处视为一种惩罚形式。

sentences.en: So in the past, it might be people being in exile, being casted out from society, even the extreme case of solitary confinement.
sentences.zh: 所以在过去，可能是人们流放、被社会抛弃，甚至是极端的单独监禁。

sentences.en: And more of the recent practice, we see things like time out that we use for children.
sentences.zh: 而在更近期的实践中，我们看到了诸如对儿童使用的暂停（time out）之类的事情。

sentences.en: So with all that, I think we discuss in the book how that might shape our idea and perceptions around solitude, and that can make it a pretty fearful experience.
sentences.zh: 综上所述，我认为我们在书中讨论了这可能会如何塑造我们对独处的想法和看法，从而使其成为一种相当令人恐惧的体验。

sentences.en: And we do see that even, like, with qualitative interview, people talking about how when they are alone in public, there's the certain feeling of being judged.
sentences.zh: 我们也确实发现，甚至在定性访谈中，人们也谈到当他们独自一人在公共场合时，有一种被评判的特定感觉。

sentences.en: People might kind of generalize the momentary solitude to who they are as a person.
sentences.zh: 人们可能会把短暂的独处概括为他们作为一个人的本质。

sentences.en: What does it mean when I don't have someone to spend time with on this Friday night, out in the city, in this restaurant?
sentences.zh: 在这个周五晚上，在城市里，在这个餐厅里，当我没有可以一起度过时光的人时，这意味着什么？

sentences.en: Does that mean I'm a loner?
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着我是个独行侠？

sentences.en: And then sometimes also, I think not just the person, but also people around us.
sentences.zh: 然后有时也是，我认为不仅是这个人，还有我们周围的人。

sentences.en: I think there's, because we talk about work in the books, how there's women sometimes out in public space might experience gays and judgment from other people.
sentences.zh: 我认为，正如我们在书中讨论的那样，女性有时在公共空间中可能会经历来自其他人的凝视和评判。

sentences.en: So yeah, so that's something that I think it's both the internalized fear, but also other people judgment as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我认为这是内化的恐惧，同时也是来自他人的评判。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think we see that as well in the language that we use for solitude.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想我们在用于独处的语言中也看到了这一点。

sentences.en: So, you know, I find that really fascinating that if we think about kind of the word solitude
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我发现这真的很迷人，如果我们思考“独处”这个词，

sentences.en: and what it means and sort of reflects the way that our society treats and has treated solitude historically, but I think it also might shape the way that we think about solitude,
sentences.zh: 以及它的含义，并在某种程度上反映了我们的社会过去和现在对待独处的方式，但我认为它也可能会塑造我们对独处的思考方式，

sentences.en: that when you think about the word, it's not a word that just means being alone.
sentences.zh: 当你思考这个词时，它并不是一个仅仅意味着独自一人的词。

sentences.en: It's a very simple concept, and yet it still needs explaining.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常简单的概念，然而它仍然需要解释。

sentences.en: And that's because we tend to kind of use the same word for solitude as we do for loneliness.
sentences.zh: 那是因为我们倾向于对独处和孤独感使用同一个词。

sentences.en: We'll talk about sort of being solitary, and that can be an emotional experience of being isolated or being alone.
sentences.zh: 我们会谈论那种独处的状态，那可能是一种被孤立或独自一人的情感体验。

sentences.en: You know, and again, the loner is a person who prefers solitude.
sentences.zh: 你知道，同样地，“独行侠”（loner）是一个偏爱独处的人。

sentences.en: So there's sort of something wrong in solitude as an idea in our head, the way we symbolize it.
sentences.zh: 因此，在我们脑海中，作为概念的独处存在某种问题，即我们将其符号化的方式。

sentences.en: And in English, we have the benefit of having the word solitude and the word loneliness.
sentences.zh: 在英语中，我们很幸运拥有“solitude”（独处）和“loneliness”（孤独感）这两个词。

sentences.en: So, you know, researchers like Tweevee and I can kind of study those two things separately and think about those two things as separate.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，像崔维和我这样的研究人员可以把这两者分开研究，并把它们视为独立的两回事。

sentences.en: But in a lot of languages around the world, there aren't two words that, you know, mean solitude, the state of being alone, and then mean loneliness.
sentences.zh: 但在世界上的许多语言中，并没有两个分别表示“独处”（独自一人的状态）和“孤独感”的词。

sentences.en: There's one word that's used interchangeably for both.
sentences.zh: 只有一个词可以互换着用于这两种情况。

sentences.en: So we don't even have a language to speak to solitude as a neutral and even positive experience.
sentences.zh: 所以我们甚至没有一种语言来将独处谈论为一种中立甚至积极的体验。

sentences.en: That's definitely true, because I could relate that to Vietnamese.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是真的，因为我可以把它与越南语联系起来。

sentences.en: We do not have a word for solitude.
sentences.zh: 我们没有一个词来表示独处。

sentences.en: In fact, the word, every time I try to translate for my family to understand,
sentences.zh: 事实上，这个词，每当我试图向家人翻译以便让他们理解时，

sentences.en: we struggle a lot because the word itself, it just doesn't make sense to say that it's a positive state.
sentences.zh: 我们都会遇到很多困难，因为这个词本身，说它是一种积极的状态是说不通的。

sentences.en: That's interesting, and I think a lot of people don't see it in a positive light.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，我想很多人并没有以积极的眼光看待它。

sentences.en: I mean, I know there's research, for example, where people are put in a situation where they are alone,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我知道有这样的研究，例如，人们被置于独自一人的情境中，

sentences.en: and then they say, you know, they would rather give themselves electric shocks than just be by themselves.
sentences.zh: 然后他们说，你知道，他们宁愿电击自己也不愿独自待着。

sentences.en: Have you participated in research like that?
sentences.zh: 你参与过这样的研究吗？

sentences.en: We heard of the study, and it's a pretty interesting study.
sentences.zh: 我们听说过这项研究，这是一项非常有趣的研究。

sentences.en: And I think, but I think the general message from that study is more about how a lot of us are uncomfortable with the idea of sitting alone with our thoughts.
sentences.zh: 并且我认为，来自该研究的核心信息更多的是关于我们许多人对于独自一人静静思考的想法感到不自在。

sentences.en: And I think the researcher decided to demonstrate that with a more sensational kind of measures, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为研究人员决定用一种更具轰动效应的测量方法来证明这一点。

sentences.en: But, yeah, so solitude is something that's best doing rather than thinking.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，所以独处是一件做比想更好的事情。

sentences.en: And I thought that was very interesting, like just people are more comfortable having something to do when they are alone.
sentences.zh: 我认为这非常有趣，就像人们独自一人时更喜欢做点什么一样。

sentences.en: And so the question is, what is that something that we can recommend people to do?
sentences.zh: 所以问题是，我们可以建议人们做什么呢？

sentences.en: And I think Tuivi's really right on this, and just to kind of highlight that I think the evidence is showing that, especially young people, if they can be with others, you know,
sentences.zh: 我觉得崔维说得非常对，我想强调的是，证据表明，特别是年轻人，如果他们能和别人在一起，你知道，

sentences.en: they're quite happy to be with others.
sentences.zh: 他们非常乐意和别人在一起。

sentences.en: It doesn't mean that that's true for everybody all the time.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着对所有人在所有时间都如此。

sentences.en: There are times where solitude is needed, beneficial, appreciated, but there are quite a few times that it's not.
sentences.zh: 在某些时候，独处是必需的、有益的、受赏识的，但也有很多时候并非如此。

sentences.en: And for young people as well, what the research is highlighting is that if they're going to be alone,
sentences.zh: 而且对年轻人来说，研究强调的是，如果他们要一个人待着，

sentences.en: they really do prefer to be doing something versus sitting alone with your thoughts is a special form of solitude that isn't always right for everybody all the time.
sentences.zh: 他们确实更倾向于做点什么，而不是独自跟自己的思绪呆在一起——这是一种独特的独处形式，并非对所有人在所有时间都完全适用。

sentences.en: We do find as people age throughout the kind of adult lifespan, they get more comfortable both with solitude and with being alone with their thoughts.
sentences.zh: 我们确实发现，随着人们在成年期逐渐变老，他们对独处以及与自己的思绪共处会变得越来越坦然。

sentences.en: So a lot of the evidence based in younger people, we're still learning about what that means for people throughout the adult lifespan and what it means for kids.
sentences.zh: 因此，关于年轻人的很多证据，我们仍在了解它对整个人生阶段以及对孩子们意味着什么。

sentences.en: So these days, a lot of us will automatically just turn to our smartphones when we're by ourselves.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，我们很多人在独自一人时，都会情不自禁地掏出智能手机。

sentences.en: I mean, can you really experience solitude if you're scrolling through social media?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你在刷社交媒体，你真的能体验到独处吗？

sentences.en: Or do you not get the benefits of solitude if you just take out your phone when you're by yourself because you don't want to be with your thoughts?
sentences.zh: 或者说，如果你独自一人时因为不想面对自己的思绪而掏出手机，你就无法享受独处的好处了吗？

sentences.en: So I did conduct like a set of studies to look at that.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实做了一组研究来探讨这个问题。

sentences.en: And it's kind of interesting is because so far the focus of my work is about the effect of solitude on emotion.
sentences.zh: 这挺有意思的，因为到目前为止，我的工作重点一直是独处对情绪的影响。

sentences.en: So if we when we only look at that, it seems like picking up the phones, browsing through social media doesn't really take away that effect that we call the deactivation effect,
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们只看这一点，就会发现拿起手机浏览社交媒体，似乎并不会真正消除那种我们称之为“去激活效应”的影响，

sentences.en: which I mentioned earlier about the drop in those strong, high arousal emotion.
sentences.zh: 也就是我之前提到的那些强烈、高唤醒度情绪的下降。

sentences.en: So even when people sitting there, browsing on the phone, that effect still happen.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使人们坐在那里玩手机，这种效应依然会发生。

sentences.en: But what we found was just it takes away this opportunity for self-reflection.
sentences.zh: 但我们发现的是，它剥夺了自我反思的机会。

sentences.en: And that has been shown.
sentences.zh: 这一点已经得到了证实。

sentences.en: So I found that in the data that we collected, but also the researcher Virginia Thomas, she also found that in young people, how like that can interfere with self-reflection.
sentences.zh: 我在我们收集的数据中发现了这一点，研究人员弗吉尼亚·托马斯也发现，在年轻人当中，这种行为是如何干扰自我反思的。

sentences.en: And she discussed about how that can also interfere with this process of identity formation,
sentences.zh: 她探讨了这如何同时干扰自我认同的形成过程，

sentences.en: because self-reflection can be pretty crucial for that period of life when people are young and still discover themselves.
sentences.zh: 因为对于正处于年轻时期、还在探索自我的群体来说，自我反思至关重要。

sentences.en: But yeah.
sentences.zh: 不过是的。

sentences.en: Just to add to that, though, that when we think about technology use, we'll tend to kind of clump it up into one thing.
sentences.zh: 不过需要补充的是，当我们想到科技使用时，往往会把它笼统地归为一谈。

sentences.en: But actually, there are a lot of different ways to engage in social media.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，参与社交媒体的方式有很多种。

sentences.en: And so when we ask people to define solitude in research that I've done with Tweevee,
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们在我和特维共同开展的研究中请人们定义独处时，

sentences.en: that we find that people will identify solitude can be passively looking at other people's posts and things like that, kind of exploring the social world in an informational way.
sentences.zh: 我们发现人们认为独处可以是被动地浏览别人的动态之类的内容，以一种获取信息的方式探索社交世界。

sentences.en: You know, what are other people up to?
sentences.zh: 你知道，别人都在忙些什么？

sentences.en: It doesn't disrupt the sense of solitude.
sentences.zh: 这并不会破坏独处的感觉。

sentences.en: It might mean it's a different flavor of solitude.
sentences.zh: 这或许意味着这是一种不同风味的独处。

sentences.en: But actually kind of actively interacting with others through social media is a different.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，通过社交媒体与他人进行积极互动则是另一回事了。

sentences.en: Now it takes people out of solitude.
sentences.zh: 这会把人们从独处状态中拉出来。

sentences.en: So we talk both about sort of, I guess, taking in social media information,
sentences.zh: 所以我们既谈到了接收社交媒体信息，

sentences.en: but also actively engaging posting or talking to other people where it becomes much more a relational experience.
sentences.zh: 也谈到了积极参与发帖或与他人交谈，这时它更像是一种关系体验。

sentences.en: And again, these are different forms of solitude.
sentences.zh: 同样，这些都是不同形式的独处。

sentences.en: And within all those experiences, you know, I think this is one of the things that we're still learning a lot about.
sentences.zh: 在所有这些体验中，你知道，我认为这是我们仍在深入了解的事情之一。

sentences.en: But, you know, we could do those things in a way that is maybe a little more compulsive or we're doing it out of habit.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我们做这些事的方式可能带有更多强迫性，或者纯粹出于习惯。

sentences.en: We can do it more mindfully.
sentences.zh: 我们也可以用更正念的方式去做。

sentences.en: So my guess is that as we learn more about this topic, we'll learn that there are different ways to, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以我的猜测是，随着我们对这个话题了解加深，我们会知道有不同的方式，

sentences.en: have solitude moments that are maybe interspersed by social media engagement or technology engagement.
sentences.zh: 去拥有那些可能穿插着社交媒体互动或科技使用的独处时刻。

sentences.en: And some are more or less harmful or disruptive to solitude than others.
sentences.zh: 其中一些对独处的伤害或破坏性比另一些更大或更小。

sentences.en: What about reading or watching TV or even listening to a podcast?
sentences.zh: 那读书、看电视，甚至听播客呢？

sentences.en: Is that a disruption to your solitude?
sentences.zh: 这会破坏你的独处吗？

sentences.en: So that study I mentioned earlier, we did include like a reading condition.
sentences.zh: 所以刚才提到的那项研究，我们确实包含了一种阅读条件。

sentences.en: Reading is actually very compatible with positive solitude, actually, because it's to me, it's very interesting how the difference between, you know,
sentences.zh: 事实上，阅读非常契合积极的独处，因为在我看来，很有意思的是，你知道，

sentences.en: reading and kind of flipping through the page and just kind of read whatever they and use able to basically reflect on the information.
sentences.zh: 阅读、翻页以及随手阅读他们看到的任何内容，并基本上能够对这些信息进行反思，这些与别的东西有很大不同。

sentences.en: At least for me, engaging with things on social media is something a little more fast based and information keep coming in.
sentences.zh: 至少对我来说，在社交媒体上参与内容要快节奏得多，信息源源不断地涌来。

sentences.en: But a lot of time, depending on the algorithm, you might see information just being fed to you, but not in a coherent way as much as you would have in a book.
sentences.zh: 但在很多情况下，根据算法的不同，你看到的信息可能是直接喂给你的，却没有像书本那样具有连贯性。

sentences.en: So I think the type of media also have different ways to kind of like feed stimuli into you when you spend time alone.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，当你独自度过时光时，不同类型的媒体也会以不同的方式向你输入刺激。

sentences.en: And if anything,
sentences.zh: 如果非要说的话，

sentences.en: I think all these things as more of different forms of stimulation and there has been work that also show that the fact that we pick up the phone sometimes to engage in like social media or to even seek out information like what Nada mentioned can be a way to regulate stress and boredom during that time.
sentences.zh: 我认为所有这些都可以看作是不同形式的刺激，并且有研究也表明，我们有时拿起手机参与社交媒体，甚至像娜达提到的那样去寻找信息，可以成为调节当时压力和无聊感的一种方式。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I do think that this topic is very interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我确实觉得这个话题非常有趣。

sentences.en: One thing I found surprising in your research is that you found that introverts don't necessarily benefit more from solitude than extroverts.
sentences.zh: 在你的研究中，我发现挺惊讶的一点是，内向的人并没有比外向的人从独处中获得更多益处。

sentences.en: So how is our need for solitude related to introversion or extroversion or even other personality traits?
sentences.zh: 那么我们对独处的需求与内向、外向甚至其他人格特质有什么关系？

sentences.en: Well, it's hard for me to think like and answer the question about introverts because I very much still want to inveSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对内向者进行思考并回答这个问题对我和我非常想深入探讨的一样很难。

sentences.en: I'm still invested in introversion and extroversion, even though that we haven't found evidence.
sentences.zh: 我仍然对内向和外向很感兴趣，尽管我们还没有找到相关证据。

sentences.en: It's just because it's just intuitively that's what we think about when we think about spending alone is that introverts tend to.
sentences.zh: 这只是因为直觉上，当我们想到独自度过时光时，内向的人往往会……

sentences.en: So there's data supporting that introverts spend more time alone than extroverts.
sentences.zh: 因此有数据支持内向者比外向者花更多时间独处。

sentences.en: So we're talking about the quantity of solitude and social interaction.
sentences.zh: 所以我们谈论的是独处和社交互动的数量。

sentences.en: And what we haven't found.
sentences.zh: 而这是我们尚未发现的。

sentences.en: So one of the papers that Nada and I both like publish is to we didn't find the correlation between introversion,
sentences.zh: 因此，娜达和我共同发表的一篇论文指出，我们没有发现内向、

sentences.en: extroversion dimension with enjoyment of solitude or engaging with solitude for meaningful and enjoyable purpose.
sentences.zh: 外向维度与享受独处或为了有意义和愉快目的而进行独处之间存在相关性。

sentences.en: So, and then when I think about that work, it's just kind of like, well, because we don't actually have a perfect measure of introversion.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我回想这项工作时，就会觉得，好吧，因为我们实际上没有完美测量内向的方法。

sentences.en: The current measures that are common in the field usually tend to treat extroversion as someone who is talkative, energized, happy.
sentences.zh: 该领域中常见的当前测量方法通常倾向于将外向定义为健谈、充满活力、快乐。

sentences.en: When introverts are basically just when you reverse code and that's the opposite of extrovert.
sentences.zh: 而内向基本上只是反向编码，也就是外向的反面。

sentences.en: So because of that, then we don't know if when we find either no correlation or even sometime positive correlation between extroversion and enjoyment of solitude,
sentences.zh: 正因如此，当我们发现外向与享受独处之间没有相关性，甚至有时呈正相关时，我们并不清楚原因所在，

sentences.en: is that just because there's some shared variance between this idea of extroverts being a happy person?
sentences.zh: 这难道只是因为外向者是快乐的人这一观念之间存在某种共同的方差吗？

sentences.en: And then because of that, then they kind of just find themselves happy in either solitude, social interaction, or any experience that they engage in their life.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，他们在独处、社交互动或生活中经历的任何体验中都会发现自己是快乐的。

sentences.en: So that to me is more of a methodological limitation.
sentences.zh: 所以在我看来，这更多是一种方法论上的局限。

sentences.en: So because of that, we're not sure if we can speak inclusively about introversion, extroversion, and enjoyment of solitude.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，我们不确定能否确凿地讨论内向、外向与享受独处的关系。

sentences.en: Yeah, and just to add to that, because I think where quantitative studies can, you know, have you scratching your head, qualitative studies can help sometimes.
sentences.zh: 是的，补充一点，因为我认为量化研究有时会让你一头雾水，而质性研究有时能提供帮助。

sentences.en: And this is an example of that, because when we've done interviews and asked people,
sentences.zh: 这就是一个例子，因为当我们进行访谈并询问人们时：

sentences.en: so what do you think it is about you that makes you enjoy solitude for those people who said they enjoy it?
sentences.zh: 对于那些说自己享受独处的人，你认为自己身上有什么特质让你享受独处？

sentences.en: People will often say it's because I'm an introvert.
sentences.zh: 人们通常会说因为我是内向的人。

sentences.en: So people will self-identify as introverts and kind of identify that it's that characteristic within them that makes them really like solitude.
sentences.zh: 所以人们会自我认同为内向者，并认为正是他们身上的这种特质让他们真正喜欢独处。

sentences.en: But, you know, when we think about how we tend to talk about solitude in the public, we'll tend to say,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，当我们思考我们在公众中如何谈论独处时，往往会说：

sentences.en: okay, definition of solitude is somebody who gets energy from being by themselves, right?
sentences.zh: 好吧，独处的定义就是从独处中获得能量的人，对吧？

sentences.en: So definitionally, I think our common understanding of what it means to be an introvert is somebody who likes to be alone.
sentences.zh: 所以在定义上，我认为我们对内向含义的共识就是喜欢独处的人。

sentences.en: And so it makes a lot of sense that those are kind of linked in our minds.
sentences.zh: 所以这两者在我们的脑海中产生联系是非常合乎情理的。

sentences.en: And what Twivi was saying was right on,
sentences.zh: 特维刚才说的完全正确，

sentences.en: because if the way we measure it actually is measuring a lot of different characteristics about us that kind of have very little to do with that,
sentences.zh: 因为如果我们测量的方式实际上在衡量与此关系甚微的许多不同特质，

sentences.en: then each of those might affect our relationship with solitude in different ways.
sentences.zh: 那么其中每一个特质都可能以不同的方式影响我们与独处的关系。

sentences.en: Now, you mentioned earlier differences in enjoyment of solitude based on people's age.
sentences.zh: 刚才你提到根据人们年龄的不同，享受独处的程度也有所差异。

sentences.en: What about other demographic differences?
sentences.zh: 那其他人口统计学差异呢？

sentences.en: Do men enjoy solitude more than women or vice versa?
sentences.zh: 男性比女性更享受独处，还是反过来？

sentences.en: Do we know?
sentences.zh: 我们知道吗？

sentences.en: Well, it's interesting because when we wrote the book, we talked about this.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这很有趣，因为我们在写书时讨论过这个问题。

sentences.en: We, and then I think the three of us kind of really try to advocate solitude practice for women as well, so that you kind of see that a little bit of that advocacy in the book,
sentences.zh: 我们，而且我认为我们三个真的试图倡导女性也进行独处实践，所以你会在书中看到一点这种倡导的影子，

sentences.en: because we tend to, mainly because we tend to get questions from people that, you know, men being independent, women being interdependent.
sentences.zh: 因为我们倾向于，主要是因为我们经常听到人们的提问：男性是独立的，女性是互依的。

sentences.en: So maybe men would be someone who enjoy time alone more, you know, talking about the idea of like the man cave and the bachelor being in his apartment or flat.
sentences.zh: 所以也许男性会是更享受独处时光的人，你知道，谈到“男人的专属空间”以及单身汉住在自己的公寓或平房里的概念。

sentences.en: But then when we look at history and also like description, there are women who, there's hermits that are women.
sentences.zh: 但当我们审视历史和描述时，会发现女性中也有隐士。

sentences.en: I think there's a word we use in the book, but I don't remember what it is, Nana.
sentences.zh: 我想我们在书里用过一个词，但我记不清是什么了，娜娜。

sentences.en: For female hermits.
sentences.zh: 指女性隐士的词。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah, and so, but the interesting thing when you think about gender, and actually often when we talk about solitude,
sentences.zh: 是的，所以，但当你思考性别时，有趣的是，通常在我们谈论独处时，

sentences.en: is that it's almost like you have to be a special kind of person to deserve solitude.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像你必须是一个特殊的人才配得上独处。

sentences.en: So a lot of these stories, and I think that's especially true for women historically,
sentences.zh: 因此，许多这样的故事，我认为历史上对女性而言尤其如此，

sentences.en: is that a woman who sort of is kind of psychologically strong enough to handle solitude and not be corrupted or, you know, weakened by it in some way,
sentences.zh: 就是一个在心理上足够强大能够应对独处、不被其腐蚀或以某种方式削弱的女性，

sentences.en: it has to be kind of, you know, spiritually already pretty transcendent.
sentences.zh: 在精神上必须已经相当超然。

sentences.en: So it's not for like the everyday person, even in those instances where we have these amazing role models.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不适合普通人，哪怕我们在现实中有这些了不起的榜样。

sentences.en: And when you look at women historically who've really kind of talked about solitude being important to them, they've sort of lived on the edge of society.
sentences.zh: 当你回顾历史上那些真正谈论独处对她们很重要的女性时，她们多半生活在社会的边缘。

sentences.en: So it's this kind of interesting thing, I think, with gender, but I think also in terms of how we think about solitude,
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这在性别方面是一个很有趣的现象，但我也认为在我们如何看待独处这一点上，

sentences.en: you know, that we tend to kind of think about this exceptional kind of transformative experience.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们往往会把它看作一种非凡的、变革性的体验。

sentences.en: It's not accessible to many of us.
sentences.zh: 并非我们大多数人都能触及。

sentences.en: And yeah, for me, that's just always striking, given how familiar it is to all of us,
sentences.zh: 是的，对我来说，鉴于这对我们所有人来说都是如此熟悉，

sentences.en: that then we have the split in the way we think about it and the way that we're all experiencing it.
sentences.zh: 却在我们的看法和所有人的实际体验之间存在这种分裂，这总是让我感到震惊。

sentences.en: And just to speak to the kind of question of how do our different backgrounds affect us,
sentences.zh: 就我们的不同背景如何影响我们这个问题而言，

sentences.en: and, you know, Tweevi might also know more about this and where the literature is out with it now,
sentences.zh: 你知道，特维可能也对此以及目前相关文献的进展了解更多，

sentences.en: but from the studies that we've done and the kind of evidence we reviewed when we were writing the book,
sentences.zh: 但根据我们做过的研究以及我们在写书时回顾的证据，

sentences.en: the takeaway is really that there are no simple answers to kind of solitude being, for example, for individualist cultures, but not collectivist cultures, it seems to be, you know,
sentences.zh: 得出的结论其实是，对于独处是否例如只适用于个人主义文化而不适用于集体主义文化，并没有简单的答案，它似乎被

sentences.en: recognized as kind of potentially having these benefits globally.
sentences.zh: 全球范围内普遍认为可能具有这些益处。

sentences.en: It's also something that globally cultures might struggle with this.
sentences.zh: 这也是全球不同文化可能都在挣扎的事情。

sentences.en: So there's this kind of, you know, shared experience.
sentences.zh: 所以存在这样一种共同的体验。

sentences.en: And I think we're only beginning to understand what that shared experience really is across the globe.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我们才刚开始了解这种共同体验在全球范围内究竟是什么。

sentences.en: And even for women where it's not, you know, always very socially accepted to be alone,
sentences.zh: 甚至对女性而言，独自一人并不总是被社会广泛接受，

sentences.en: you know, you hear stories of kind of women even in the home taking a few minutes on their own,
sentences.zh: 你知道，你会听到一些女性的故事，甚至在家里也会留出几分钟属于自己的时间，

sentences.en: even when they're meant to be sort of 24 hours on call for the kids and taking care of the family.
sentences.zh: 哪怕她们本该24小时随叫随地照顾孩子和家庭。

sentences.en: So, you know, I think people have taken those at least brief moments to find solitude in everyday life
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我认为人们至少抓住了这些短暂的时刻，在日常生活中寻找独处，

sentences.en: and that it doesn't seem to be, as far as we can tell so far, culturally specific or bound to any specific kind of time in our lives or subgroup.
sentences.zh: 就我们目前所能了解的而言，它似乎并不是特定于文化的，也不受限于我们生活中的某个特定时期或某个亚群体。

sentences.en: Do people who were only children have more of a craving for solitude than those who grew up with siblings or do we not know?
sentences.zh: 独生子女比那些在兄弟姐妹陪伴下长大的人对独处有更强烈的渴望吗，还是我们并不清楚？

sentences.en: I don't think we know anything really.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们真的什么都不知道。

sentences.en: But we do have some hypothesis around how development can shape people's relationship with solitude.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实有一些关于成长经历如何塑造人们与独处关系的假设。

sentences.en: And that's specifically related to the work of Donald Winnicott when he talked about the capacity being alone, being built throughout the person development.
sentences.zh: 这具体与唐纳德·温尼科特的观点有关，他谈到独处能力是在个人成长过程中建立起来的。

sentences.en: How, you know, if a child has more opportunities to engage with solitude.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果一个孩子有更多机会进行独处。

sentences.en: So he talked about how perhaps when the mom or primary caregiver being away and doing some tasks next to the child,
sentences.zh: 所以他谈到，也许当母亲或主要照顾者离开并在孩子旁边做一些杂务时，

sentences.en: but the child get the opportunities to explore the environment and kind of just be alone in that space and feel safe.
sentences.zh: 但孩子有机会探索周围环境，并在那个空间里独自呆着并感到安全。

sentences.en: Then that becomes a practice later on when the child grows up and also have a more healthy relationship with solitude.
sentences.zh: 那么这就成为孩子长大后的一种习惯，并与独处建立起更健康的 RELATIONSHIP（关系）。

sentences.en: So we have seen literatures that talk about that, whether or not that has been tested.
sentences.zh: 所以我们已经看到过探讨这一点的文献，至于这是否得到了检验。

sentences.en: I think that would be something I'm not aware that anyone has tracked it longitudinally.
sentences.zh: 我想据我所知，还没有人进行过纵向追踪研究。

sentences.en: I think the closest we have is qualitative work.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们最接近的是质性研究。

sentences.en: That's really even even then it's really early, early stages, qualitative work where people do talk about their early experiences shaping their relationship with solitude.
sentences.zh: 即使在那时，这也确实处于非常非常早期的阶段，即通过质性研究人们确实会谈论早期经历如何塑造他们与独处的关系。

sentences.en: You know, but they will talk both about having big families where, OK, then I needed to seek out the space for myself and also being, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，但他们会谈到既有大家庭，好吧，那我需要为自己寻找空间，也有

sentences.en: the only child in the house and then having to learn to play by themselves.
sentences.zh: 屋里只有自己一个孩子，然后必须学会自己一个人玩。

sentences.en: So it seems like our environment shapes our relationship in some way, but that we're bringing something into how it does that, you know, it's kind of separate.
sentences.zh: 所以看起来我们的环境在某种程度上塑造了我们的关系，但我们在其中发挥的作用又是相对独立的。

sentences.en: There isn't a sort of one kind of the right amount of siblings or household members or privacy to be a sort of person who appreciates solitude.
sentences.zh: 并没有说兄弟姐妹、家庭成员或隐私达到某种特定的数量或程度，就能让人成为一个懂得欣赏独处的人。

sentences.en: Oh, I want to kind of mention a story I read this week, actually, by someone sharing on Twitter, a thread about how her development has shaped our relationship with solitude.
sentences.zh: 哦，其实我想顺便提一个我这周读到的故事，是有人在推特上分享的一个话题串，关于她的成长经历是如何塑造她与独处的关系的。

sentences.en: And she mentioned about the idea of how if, you know, you are someone who grow up with parents whenever you do something wrong and you get put in time out.
sentences.zh: 她提到了这样一个想法：如果你是一个每当做错事就被父母关禁闭的小孩。

sentences.en: It's not really a way for you to develop that healthy relationship with solitude.
sentences.zh: 这其实并不是让你培养与独处建立健康关系的方式。

sentences.en: And I thought that was really insightful.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这真的很有见地。

sentences.en: I think that kind of ties to the what we have talked about, about how these norms that we carry around this idea of solitude and how that can be shaped by our society,
sentences.zh: 我认为这与我们之前讨论过的内容不谋而合，即我们周围承载的关于独处的这些规范是如何被社会所塑造的，

sentences.en: but also our development as well.
sentences.zh: 同时也受到我们自身成长的影响。

sentences.en: And yeah, so I thought that's just something interesting to share.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以我认为这只是一些有趣的内容想要分享。

sentences.en: Well, talking about solitude as punishment, I mean, that is one thing that we use in prisons, for example,
sentences.zh: 嗯，说到把独处当作惩罚，我的意思是，这是我们在监狱里使用的一种方法，例如

sentences.en: where we will put people in solitary confinement for long periods of time, sometimes years and years.
sentences.zh: 我们会把人单独关押很长时间，有时甚至长达数年之久。

sentences.en: What is happening to the health of such people?
sentences.zh: 这种人的健康状况会发生什么变化？

sentences.en: What do we know about long term?
sentences.zh: 关于长期影响我们了解多少？

sentences.en: What happens to people who are in solitary?
sentences.zh: 被单独关押的人会发生什么？

sentences.en: Does everybody react to it in the same way?
sentences.zh: 每个人对它的反应都一样吗？

sentences.en: We both have a lot of things to say.
sentences.zh: 我们俩都有很多话要说。

sentences.en: I think about solitary confinement, but kind of a few, a few reactions to that.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈单独监禁，不过有几种不同的反应。

sentences.en: The first is when we talk about solitary confinement, we're actually talking in a way about isolation, especially as you talk about these extended periods of time.
sentences.zh: 首先，当我们谈论单独监禁时，某种程度上我们实际上是在谈论隔离，特别是当你谈到这些延长的禁闭时间时。

sentences.en: And one of the fascinating things when you hear people talking about kind of more extreme solitary confinement is they talk about it being a very relational experience.
sentences.zh: 当你听到人们谈论更极端的单独监禁时，最引人入胜的事情之一就是他们会谈到这是一种高度人际关系的体验。

sentences.en: So we think about people being alone, but they're put there by somebody who's sort of saying, I have power over you.
sentences.zh: 所以我们认为人们是独自一人的，但他们被关在那里是由某个人决定的，那个人相当于在说：我对你拥有权力。

sentences.en: And, you know, because you've misbehaved or you've disobeyed me in some way, I'm not pleased with you, I'm going to punish you.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，因为你行为不端或者在某种程度上违抗了我，我对你不满意，我要惩罚你。

sentences.en: So although it is solitude, it's kind of a type of isolation where that relationship with the guard becomes really salient and important.
sentences.zh: 所以虽然它是独处，但它是一种隔离，在这种隔离中，与狱警的关系变得非常突出和重要。

sentences.en: It's also often when people talk about difficult moments of solitary confinement or difficult periods, they'll tend to talk about solitary confinement that is also devoid of,
sentences.zh: 而且人们在谈论孤立监禁的艰难时刻或艰难时期时，往往也会谈到那种缺乏

sentences.en: you know, exercise, fresh air, nature, activities to keep the mind engaged, physical comfort, you know, warmth.
sentences.zh: 比如说锻炼、新鲜空气、大自然、能让大脑保持活跃的活动、物质上的舒适，也就是温暖的隔离。

sentences.en: So when we think about solitary confinement, we will tend to gravitate to really thinking about the solitude in it.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们想到孤立监禁时，往往会自然而然地把重点放在其中的“孤独”上。

sentences.en: But there's so much more that happens when people are put in solitary confinement than that they're separated from other people.
sentences.zh: 但把人们关进孤立监禁所带来的影响，远不止与其他人隔离那么简单。

sentences.en: And there's been research done with prisoners who have had short periods of solitary confinement in prisons that, you know, essentially care about prisoner rights,
sentences.zh: 针对在监狱里经历过短期孤立监禁的囚犯进行过一些研究，这些监狱你知道的，基本上是关心囚犯权益的

sentences.en: where actually they feel that's a positive break from an intense social experience, sometimes one where I feel unsafe.
sentences.zh: 在这些地方，他们实际上觉得那是一种从紧张的社交体验中抽离出来的积极休息，有时这种社交体验甚至会让我觉得不安全。

sentences.en: So I'm not saying that we should kind of put more people into solitary confinement.
sentences.zh: 所以，我并不是说我们应该把更多的人关进孤立监禁室。

sentences.en: And I think I personally don't have the expertise to say it one way or another, but I think that as well is not inherently about having some solitude time.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我个人也没有专业知识来对此妄加评论，但我认为这本身也并不单纯是为了获得一些独处时间。

sentences.en: It's about potentially having excessive, forced, and oppressive amount of solitude time and having that be paired with a sort of, you know,
sentences.zh: 这可能涉及过度、被迫且压抑的独处时间，并且这种独处往往伴随着一种，你知道的

sentences.en: kind of the aggressive relational dynamic with the people who are in charge of the prisoner, as well as the kind of day-to-day experiences of being deprived of comforts.
sentences.zh: 与监狱管理者之间充满攻击性的人际动态，以及日常生活中心灵慰藉被剥夺的体验。

sentences.en: Yeah, I agree with Neda that, like, the solitude in the context of solitary confinement is confounded by a lot of other factors around it.
sentences.zh: 是的，我同意内达的看法，孤立监禁语境下的孤独，实际上被它周围的许多其他因素所干扰了。

sentences.en: But when we, let's say we take that solitude out and just study that in the lab, so there has been a group of researchers that did that.
sentences.zh: 但假设我们把这种孤独抽离出来，单纯在实验室里进行研究——确实有一组研究人员就是这么做的。

sentences.en: And, you know, I mentioned earlier about how when they study isolation, they quantify that as 10 hours of being alone, not interacting with anyone.
sentences.zh: 而且，正如我刚才提到的，他们在研究隔离时，将其量化为10个小时独自一人、不与任何人互动。

sentences.en: So the effect of that is they show that there's a drop in our energy level.
sentences.zh: 所以这样做的结果显示，我们的精力水平会下降。

sentences.en: So, you know, of course, there's other outcomes like loneliness.
sentences.zh: 当然，除此之外还会产生其他结果，比如孤独感。

sentences.en: There's one interesting outcome that they measure is craving of social interaction.
sentences.zh: 他们测量到的一个有趣的结果是，人们对社交互动的渴望。

sentences.en: So that all makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这一切都说得通。

sentences.en: But the drop in energy level, I find that very interesting is because if we're talking about the fact of momentary solitude is drop in our strong emotion,
sentences.zh: 但精力水平的下降，我觉得非常有趣，因为如果我们讨论的是短暂的独处会导致我们强烈情感的消退

sentences.en: then the extended period of that, that can have some implication for our energy.
sentences.zh: 那么长时间的独处可能会对我们的精力产生一些影响。

sentences.en: And if we think of ourselves as an organism that we do need, like, you know, a balanced energy level, talk about homeostasis,
sentences.zh: 如果我们认为自己是一个确实需要保持平衡的精力水平的生物，也就是内稳态

sentences.en: then that can't be good if, you know, a prolonged period and then our energy drop down and the implication of that.
sentences.zh: 那么如果经历很长时间，我们的精力下降，并且产生相应的后果，那绝对不是什么好事。

sentences.en: So I think when we think about solitude and distinguish that from isolation, which is an extended period,
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为当我们思考独处并将其与隔离（这是一种较长时间的状态）区分开来时

sentences.en: when we are cut off from social network and connection, I think that the length of time is pretty determining factors.
sentences.zh: 当我们被切断与社会网络和联系的纽带时，我认为持续的时间是一个相当关键的决定因素。

sentences.en: There is that if short period, you can talk about it as calm and relaxation, but then long period, that can't be good.
sentences.zh: 如果是短期的，你可以称之为平静和放松，但如果是长期的，那就绝不会是好事。

sentences.en: Just like anything, I think it's all about balance.
sentences.zh: 就像任何事情一样，我认为关键全在于平衡。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Just to change gears a little bit, back in the late 90s, the early 2000s, there was a lot of discussion about this idea that was dubbed Bowling Alone,
sentences.zh: 换个话题，在上世纪90年代末到2000年代初，曾有很多关于一个被称为“独自保龄球”的观点的讨论

sentences.en: which eventually became a book, and Robert Putnam, who was the author, he noted how people were becoming less and less involved in face-to-face social interactions.
sentences.zh: 这个观点后来成了一本书，作者罗伯特·帕特南指出，人们参与面对面社交互动的频次越来越低。

sentences.en: Is there any scientific evidence that we're becoming more solitary?
sentences.zh: 有没有任何科学证据表明我们变得越来越孤立了？

sentences.en: And if so, is that a problem?
sentences.zh: 如果是这样，这算是一个问题吗？

sentences.en: I don't know of any evidence that would suggest that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道有任何证据能表明这一点。

sentences.en: You know, I think the nature of our relationships is changing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为我们的人际关系性质正在发生变化。

sentences.en: Arguably, this isn't the first time that it's changed.
sentences.zh: 可以说，这并不是人际关系性质第一次发生改变了。

sentences.en: You know, I don't think humans have been holding their relationship kind of steady for 2,000 years,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不认为人类的社会关系已经稳定维持了2000年

sentences.en: and all of a sudden, you know, the last 20 years have happened and we're kind of fundamentally different.
sentences.zh: 然后突然之间，在过去的20年里发生了变化，我们就变得从根本上不同了。

sentences.en: I think probably our relationships are always changing in the nature that we relate to others in our community, our families.
sentences.zh: 我想我们与社区、家庭中他人交往的性质可能一直都在改变。

sentences.en: So we're seeing shifts in the way that we relate, but at least I haven't seen any compelling evidence that we're kind of fundamentally becoming less sociable.
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到了交往方式的转变，但至少我还没有看到任何令人信服的证据，证明我们从根本上变得越来越不爱社交了。

sentences.en: I think our sense of connection to other people is extremely important.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们与他人的连接感极其重要。

sentences.en: I don't think anybody would argue with that.
sentences.zh: 我想没有人会反驳这一点。

sentences.en: And it continues to be the case.
sentences.zh: 而且情况一直如此。

sentences.en: So people will pursue opportunities for connecting with other people in the best ways that they know how.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们会用他们所知道的最好方式去追求与他人连接的机会。

sentences.en: The statistic that I'm aware of is just there's an increase in single-person household.
sentences.zh: 我所了解到的统计数据是，单人家庭的数量确实在增加。

sentences.en: And usually that also tends to be mentioned in relation to the loneliness epidemic.
sentences.zh: 而且这通常也会与孤独流行病联系在一起被提及。

sentences.en: But there's one argument by a sociologist that I found really compelling was that he was talking about how that could be a correlation,
sentences.zh: 但有一位社会学家的观点让我觉得非常有说服力，他指出这可能只是一种相关性

sentences.en: but that doesn't mean it's a causation is because we might have, you know, the loneliness epidemic going on and we see more people.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着存在因果关系，因为我们可能正经历孤独流行病，而且我们看到更多这样的人。

sentences.en: Part of that we don't know is just because we become more aware of loneliness, aware of the issues around mental health, and we see more of that being reported.
sentences.zh: 部分原因我们并不清楚，可能只是因为我们对孤独有了更多的认识，对心理健康相关的问题有了更多的了解，所以我们看到了更多这样的报道。

sentences.en: But in terms of the increase in single adult household, he was talking about how in the past we kind of tend to have to rely on each other more for resources.
sentences.zh: 但就单身成年家庭的增加而言，他谈到过去我们在资源上往往更倾向于依赖彼此。

sentences.en: And now there are, at least in developing societies, and we do see evidence of more single adult household in developing societies.
sentences.zh: 而现在，至少在发展中社会，我们确实看到了更多单身成年家庭的证据。

sentences.en: It's just because there are social services, there are more resources in terms of financial capability for people that allow people to live alone.
sentences.zh: 这只是因为有了社会服务，人们在财务能力方面有了更多资源，从而允许人们独自生活。

sentences.en: So I think a lot of that, there's other sociological factors that might explain that as well.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为其中很大一部分原因，可能还有其他社会学因素可以解释。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So what's next for you both?
sentences.zh: 那么你们接下来有什么打算？

sentences.en: What are you researching now?
sentences.zh: 你们现在在研究什么？

sentences.en: You know, when we think about kind of solitude, for me, it's a place to build that relationship with yourself.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我们思考独处时，对我来说，这是一个建立与自我关系的地方。

sentences.en: And we're just learning about that.
sentences.zh: 而我们才刚刚开始了解这一点。

sentences.en: And if you think about going out and having a conversation with somebody else, they could be really unkind to you, or they could be really kind, supportive, or unsupportive,
sentences.zh: 如果你考虑走出去和别人对话，他们可能会对很不友好，或者可能会非常亲切、支持你，或者不支持你

sentences.en: listen to your feelings or not.
sentences.zh: 倾听你的感受或是不倾听。

sentences.en: I think we can do the same kinds of things with ourselves in that it's that relationship in much the same way that you can be a good or bad friend.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们也可以对自己做同样的事情，就像你可以成为一个好朋友或坏朋友一样，这种关系也是如此。

sentences.en: Whether we're good or bad friends to ourselves really could make a difference.
sentences.zh: 我们对自己是好朋友还是坏朋友，确实会产生很大的影响。

sentences.en: We're kind of exploring those aspects of solitude and also examining more about technology and what does it mean to pepper your solitude with social media time or have social media time intrude in solitude space?
sentences.zh: 我们正在探索独处的这些方面，同时也更多地研究科技，以及用社交媒体时间来点缀你的独处时间，或者让社交媒体时间侵入独处空间，这究竟意味着什么？

sentences.en: Can it have certain benefits and certain costs?
sentences.zh: 它会带来某些好处和某些代价吗？

sentences.en: So one of the things that we're seeing is when we go on social media, it helps satisfy our relatedness need is the way we talk about it.
sentences.zh: 我们发现的一个现象是，当我们刷社交媒体时，它有助于满足我们的归属感需求，我们是这么称呼它的。

sentences.en: We feel a sense of connection to other people.
sentences.zh: 我们会感受到与其他人的连接感。

sentences.en: And that might help to explain why people are, you know,
sentences.zh: 这或许可以解释为什么人们，你知道的

sentences.en: when they're in solitude or kind of jumping out of it and dipping into easy social interactions that they can have from the comfort of their couch or, you know,
sentences.zh: 当他们在独处时，或者某种程度上跳出独处，沉浸在可以从舒适的沙发上，或者你知道的

sentences.en: wherever they happen to be.
sentences.zh: 无论他们身在何处，就能轻松获得的社交互动中时，会有这样的表现。

sentences.en: And sort of what that means in terms of both potential costs and benefits.
sentences.zh: 以及这在潜在代价和收益方面意味着什么。

sentences.en: And so I think those kinds of questions are really, really intriguing to understand how to sort of optimize their solitude time and also what can make it difficult.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这些问题真的非常引人入胜，有助于我们理解如何优化他们的独处时间，以及是什么让独处变得困难。

sentences.en: Yeah, for me, I'm kind of really fascinated about the idea of studying solitude and how that become like a kind of just like an essential part of our humanity.
sentences.zh: 是的，对我来说，我真的很着迷于研究独处这个概念，以及它是如何成为我们人性中不可或缺的一部分的。

sentences.en: Just because I think for a while we tend to think of ourselves as social animal.
sentences.zh: 只是因为我觉得有一段时间我们倾向于把自己视为社会性动物。

sentences.en: And because of that, intuitively, we tend to think of when we're without other people, when we're alone, and it's kind of like the opposite of that.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，直觉上我们往往认为，当我们没有和别人在一起、当我们独处时，这就好比是社交的对立面。

sentences.en: So for a while, solitude doesn't fit into the idea of us as being social animal.
sentences.zh: 所以在一段时间里，独处并不符合我们作为社会性动物的定义。

sentences.en: So I think next for me, it's just kind of to dig into that idea and challenge it a little more and like with and just naturally,
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得我接下来要做的事，就是深入探讨这个观点并对其进行更多挑战，而且很自然地

sentences.en: I tend to just gravitate it toward experimental design.
sentences.zh: 我往往会倾向于实验设计。

sentences.en: And we kind of try to, for example, right now, thinking about how if solitude brings down our emotion.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们现在正试图探讨，如果独处能平复我们的情绪。

sentences.en: So in a stressful situation, what does that look like?
sentences.zh: 那么在压力情境下，情况会是怎样的？

sentences.en: And what are the factors that might play into that?
sentences.zh: 有哪些因素可能会在其中起作用？

sentences.en: Like you said earlier, there are situations where those strong emotions might come up again when we are alone.
sentences.zh: 就像你刚才说的，在某些情况下，当我们独处时，那些强烈的情感可能会再次涌现。

sentences.en: But what contribute to that?
sentences.zh: 但究竟是什么导致了这一点？

sentences.en: Is it something that's going on in our thoughts, in the behaviors that we do when we are alone?
sentences.zh: 是我们在独处时脑海中的想法，还是我们的行为？

sentences.en: So to me, right now, we try to zoom in and kind of just say like, what can we learn more about solitude to explain why we spend time alone,
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，现在我们试图聚焦并简单地说：关于独处，我们还能学到什么，从而解释我们为什么要花时间独处

sentences.en: if it is indeed that we are social animal?
sentences.zh: 如果我们确实是社会性动物的话？

sentences.en: I think just to add kind of a big picture, you know,
sentences.zh: 我想补充一点宏观层面的、你知道的

sentences.en: intriguing thing about the topic is one of the things that solitude researchers are sort of highlighting is that a good day and maybe a kind of good life experiencing well-being that comes from having the very best of social relationships and the very best of solitude.
sentences.zh: 这个话题最吸引人的地方在于，独处研究人员强调的一点是：美好的一天，或许还有美好的人生、以及源于拥有最好的人际关系和最好的独处所带来的幸福感。

sentences.en: So if we can take those two contexts for everyday life and sort of optimize them for ourselves, that's where we can gain the most well-being.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我们能将日常生活中的这两种情境为自己进行优化，这正是我们获得最多幸福感的地方。

sentences.en: And some of that is, you know, how do they live in balance with one another?
sentences.zh: 其中一部分，你知道的，是它们如何彼此保持平衡？

sentences.en: So we're having the right kind of amounts for us.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们如何拥有适合自己的适度时间。

sentences.en: But also, what do we do during that time?
sentences.zh: 还有，我们在那段时间里做什么？

sentences.en: How do we take advantage of it?
sentences.zh: 我们如何利用好它？

sentences.en: And, you know, for me, it's just really intriguing because so Tweevi and I are both kind of social psychologists, clinical backgrounds.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对我来说，这真的很迷人，因为苏薇和我都是社会心理学家，有临床背景。

sentences.en: We're very much tied into the social world.
sentences.zh: 我们与社交世界有着非常紧密的联系。

sentences.en: And can we come from a field where the interest is in relationships?
sentences.zh: 我们是否来自于一个对人际关系感兴趣的领域？

sentences.en: How are we with others?
sentences.zh: 我们如何对待他人？

sentences.en: How are others with us?
sentences.zh: 他人如何对待我们？

sentences.en: And so psychologists have worked a lot to learn about that part of our lives.
sentences.zh: 因此，心理学家做了大量工作来了解我们生活中的那一部分。

sentences.en: But there's this whole other world of solitude that actually we know so little about.
sentences.zh: 但还有一个全新的独处世界，其实我们对此知之甚少。

sentences.en: There's so little research in this area.
sentences.zh: 这个领域的研究太少了。

sentences.en: So few solitude researchers compared to the relationships researchers that are out there.
sentences.zh: 与现有的关系研究人员相比，研究独处的人少之又少。

sentences.en: So, you know, I think it's just an area where there are a lot of questions still and we're learning a lot all the time.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我认为这是一个仍有许多疑问的领域，我们一直在不断学习。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, it makes it a really kind of exciting, intriguing and mysterious area of study.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这使得它成为一个非常令人兴奋、引人入胜且充满神秘色彩的研究领域。

sentences.en: Well, this has been really interesting.
sentences.zh: 好了，这次访谈真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: I want to thank you both for joining me and I wish you great luck and success in your future research endeavors.
sentences.zh: 我要感谢两位参加我们的节目，并祝愿你们未来的研究工作好运连连、取得成功。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。
